title: Scheduled Maintenance Orchestration and Quiesce Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook describes the recommended orchestration, safety checks, and rollback procedures for scheduled maintenance windows on Private Deployments (VPC and on-prem). It covers quiesce strategies for model-serving nodes, tenant-aware maintenance sequencing, traffic shaping, telemetry expectations, and operator run steps. The goal is to minimize customer-facing errors, meet SLO targets during maintenance, and provide deterministic rollback points.

Target audience:
- Field operators and SREs performing scheduled maintenance
- Customer success engineering (CSE) involved in customer-facing notifications
- On-prem installers and partner operators

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Redwood Private deployments with the unified control plane and per-customer tenant isolation.
- Assumes the deployment uses the standard Redwood runtime (service names: rwd-ingest, rwd-runtime, rwd-router, rwd-kvstore, rwd-telemetry).
- Assumes telemetry-forwarding (syslog/HTTP) is operational to central observability prior to window.

Definitions and key SLOs to preserve during maintenance:
- 99th percentile generation latency (p99): target <= 4000ms during maintenance for critical tenants (news/finance).
- Error rate (5xx) increase tolerated: <= 1% absolute increase over baseline for the maintenance window.
- Change freeze: no model swaps or schema migrations during maintenance unless part of the planned activity.

High-level maintenance patterns (choose one):
1) Rolling-quiesce (recommended): Drain traffic from a subset of nodes, perform maintenance, rejoin nodes, repeat. Preserves capacity for traffic routing fallback.
2) Capacity-swap (for air-gapped or limited-hardware sites): Provision temporary replacement nodes (ephemeral nodes) and shift traffic, then remove old nodes.
3) Network-isolate mode (for deep network upgrades): Pause tenant egress paths and run maintenance with customer pre-acknowledgement; higher customer coordination required.

Pre-window checklist (operator must verify):
- Stakeholders notified: CSE, customer contacts (if required), oncall SRE, and release owner.
- Backups: KV-store snapshots completed and stored to the approved retention vault.
- Health baseline: capture live metrics for 15 minutes (CPU/GPU utilization, request rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate). Attach snapshot to the maintenance ticket.
- Canary plan and smoke tests defined: include prompt set with at least 20 representative prompts and expected token-length distribution.
- Rollback anchors created: tag container images and save runtime checkpoint identifier (KV snapshot id).

Communication template (for customer-facing windows):
- Title: "Redwood Private maintenance window for <customer> - <date>"
- Body: include start/end time (UTC), expected impact (e.g., "no downtime for best-effort tenants; possible 5–10s latency increase for critical tenants"), contact escalation, and the runbook link.

Detailed operator run steps (Rolling-quiesce pattern):
1) Start window and confirm required personnel availability.
2) Verify baseline metrics recorded.
3) On rwd-router, mark node set A as Drain: `rwdctl node drain --group A --grace-period 120`
4) Wait until in-flight requests on group A drop below 2% of normal load (monitor rwd-router.metrics.inflight).
5) On nodes in group A perform maintenance action (example: OS kernel update or CUDA driver upgrade):
   a) `sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y linux-image-5.19`
   b) restart container runtime: `systemctl restart docker`
   c) run runtime self-check: `rwd-runtime healthcheck --full` (exit 0 expected)
6) Rejoin nodes: `rwdctl node undrain --group A` and confirm they pass health probes for 3 consecutive health checks.
7) Repeat for next node group.
8) After all groups completed, run post-maintenance smoke tests against the canary prompt set and verify metric deltas are within thresholds.

Quiesce best practices and caveats:
- KV cache preservation: Before draining, persist live KV shards to disk and notify controller to persist to central S3/GCS endpoint. Command: `rwd-kvctl snapshot --shard all --dest s3://tenant-backups/<tenant>/<ts>`
- Avoid trimming model KV caches unless justified; rebuilding caches can incur high p99 spikes.
- Streaming sessions: notify active long-lived streaming sessions and keep a small buffer of nodes for session continuity. Consider graceful transfer: `rwd-router session migrate --target-group B --timeout 30`
- GPU drivers and CUDA: full node reboot required for driver updates. Schedule those for maintenance groups with at least 2x redundancy.

Telemetry and acceptance criteria (post-window):
- Runbook completion artifacts: attach KV snapshot IDs, image tags, terminal logs, and smoke test results to the maintenance ticket.
- Acceptance checks (all must pass):
  - p99 latency no worse than +25% of baseline for non-critical tenants; critical tenants must be <= +10% of baseline.
  - No increase in 5xx > 1% absolute.
  - Successful completion of 100% smoke tests for canary prompt set.
  - All nodes reporting `rwd-runtime` verson/build matching deployed image tag.

Rollback and emergency stop procedure:
1) If error rate or latency exceeds rollback thresholds during maintenance, initiate emergency stop.
2) Emergency stop steps:
   a) Pause remaining scheduled steps in orchestration engine: `rwd-orch pause-window --id <window-id>`
   b) If a node group's update caused regression, mark the group out-of-service and revert image:
      - `rwdctl node set-image --group A --image rwd-runtime:<previous-tag>`
      - `rwdctl node undrain --group A` after image revert and healthcheck.
   c) If KV corruption suspected, restore KV snapshot: `rwd-kvctl restore --snapshot-id <id>` and restart affected services.
3) Notify stakeholders and open a postmortem ticket if the rollback was non-trivial.

Example maintenance matrix (sampling):
- Small customer site (<= 4 GPUs): use Capacity-swap pattern, maintenance window 2 hours, target: single-pass reimage.
- Mid-size (8–32 GPUs): Rolling-quiesce with groups of 2–4 nodes, window 4–8 hours.
- Large (>= 64 GPUs): Rolling-quiesce with automated orchestration, prepare hot-spare nodes for capacity-swap in case of prolonged reboots.

Operational automation snippets (YAML job example):
```
# Orchestration job (K8s CronJob style simplified)
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: rwd-maintain-group-a
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: maint-step
        image: rwd/orchestrator:stable
        args: ["node-drain", "--group", "A", "--grace", "120"]
      restartPolicy: Never
```

Post-window review checklist (within 48 hours):
- Confirm metrics returned to baseline or acceptable delta.
- Archive telemetry snapshots and attach to the change ticket.
- Update runbook with any new troubleshooting steps discovered.
- If rollback performed, schedule a follow-up root-cause analysis with SRE and the release owner.

Ownership and escalation:
- Runbook owner: Eng Private Deployments SRE (primary: oncall-eng-private@s.redwood.ai).
- Change approver: Release Manager (product).
- Escalation path: operator -> oncall SRE -> SRE lead -> Eng Director. Include phone and pager details in the maintenance ticket.

Appendix A: Sample smoke tests (CLI):
1) Basic generation test: `rwdctl generate --model rwd-7b --prompt-file smoke/prompts.txt --timeout 15` expected exit 0 and average latency < 1s for short prompts.
2) Long form test: `rwdctl generate --model rwd-7b --prompt "Explain quantum entanglement" --max-tokens 512` verify no tokenization errors and final status COMPLETE.

Appendix B: Known risks and mitigations:
- Risk: KV cache rebuild causes p99 spike. Mitigation: schedule per-tenant cache warmup and use traffic mirroring to pre-fill caches.
- Risk: Driver update causes nodal boot loops. Mitigation: validate driver image on a staging node with identical hardware profile before production group.
